item.title: DigiCert admits 16-month security lapse exposed customer information
item.description: DigiCert has admitted that a botched server migration left an internal system exposed to the internet for more than a year, allowing an unauthorized user to access customer data, including passports, driver's licenses, and other identity documents. The certificate authority has begun notifying affected customers but has yet to disclose how many people had their information exposed. In an email seen by The Register , DigiCert confirmed the compromised information included names, business email addresses, phone numbers, and business addresses. Some records may also have contained passports, driver's licenses, utility bills, or other identification documents. "We are completing a review of identification documents to determine the specific individuals involved," DigiCert told those affected, adding that it would notify those people once the review was complete. DigiCert's incident report traces the blunder back to February 2025, when an internal business system was moved from a VPN-protected network to a different availability zone. That change also opened the system up to the public internet, where it sat for more than 16 months without DigiCert realizing. The archive used the same account management platform as DigiCert's customer-facing products, including a self-registration feature that was never supposed to be available on the internal system. This allowed outsiders to create accounts without multifactor authentication and, thanks to a separate permissions flaw, use them to browse archived customer records. DigiCert found the unauthorized accounts on June 18, 2026, but initially dismissed them as harmless because they weren't assigned to an application. A security researcher raised the alarm about the account creation issue three days later, but it took until July 2 for DigiCert to shut it down. Unfortunately, someone had already been poking around. It wasn't until October 12 that DigiCert began investigating whether customer information had actually been accessed. On October 19, it confirmed that an unauthorized account had accessed a subset of archived records between June 27 and July 2. DigiCert described the affected records as a "small proportion" of its archive but hasn't disclosed how many customers or individuals were caught up in the breach. The company did not respond to The Register ’s questions at the time of publication. DigiCert's postmortem makes for uncomfortable reading. The server move didn't get a proper security review, monitoring failed to pick up suspicious activity, and the access controls weren't much use against self-registered accounts. The company has since switched off self-registration, tightened network access, and added monitoring that might have come in handy a few months earlier. Certificate authority operations, CertCentral, and DigiCert ONE were unaffected, the company said, adding that customer credentials and issued certificates remain secure. item.title: Today in Motorsport History, November 6: Melandri Beat Hayden by 0.097s at Valencia in 2005 as Rossi Charged From 15th to Third
item.description: A rider on a white sports bike. Illustrative image, not from the 2005 season finale. Photo: Byron Sullivan / Pexels Marco Melandri beat Nicky Hayden by 0.097 seconds at Valencia 21 years ago today, on November 6, 2005, in the last race of a MotoGP season whose champion had already been settled. Valentino Rossi, who clinched his fifth straight premier-class title at Sepang six weeks earlier, started 15th after a qualifying crash and still finished third. The 2005 Valencia MotoGP finale was a race with nothing on the line for the title, and it still produced one of the closest finishes of the year. A title already decided, a runner-up fight still open Rossi wrapped up the 2005 championship at the Malaysian Grand Prix on September 25, finishing second to Loris Capirossi while his only remaining challenger, Max Biaggi, ended up sixth. It was his fifth consecutive premier-class crown (one in 500cc and four in MotoGP) and his seventh world title overall, according to Crash.net’s race report . That left second place in the standings as the live fight, and it was between two Hondas. Melandri arrived having won in Turkey the race before. He had climbed from 15th in the 2003 standings and 12th in 2004, and another win would secure second place in the championship. Hayden, the Repsol Honda rider, was chasing his best season yet after finishing fifth and eighth in his first two years in the class. What happened at Valencia Fact Detail Date Sunday, November 6, 2005 Event Valencian Community Grand Prix, final round of the 2005 MotoGP season Circuit Circuit Ricardo Tormo, Valencia, Spain MotoGP pole Sete Gibernau (1:31.874) Winner Marco Melandri, Movistar Honda (46:58.152) Margin 0.097s over Nicky Hayden, Repsol Honda Third Valentino Rossi, Yamaha, from 15th on the grid (+2.959s) Attendance 124,520, reported as a sell-out 2005 Valencian Community Grand Prix, MotoGP class. Sources: Crash.net race report; Wikipedia race entry; Road Racing World. Gibernau took pole for the fifth time that season, but his race was over within a few laps with an engine failure. Melandri led from the first corner and Hayden stayed on his tail for the whole 30 laps, on a circuit where overtaking is hard. Melandri opened a small gap, then had a bobble before the final corner that let Hayden close right up. Hayden went for the pass on the exit, and Melandri held his line to take the win. Melandri said afterward it was “a dream come true,” per Road Racing World . A rider on a white sports bike. Illustrative image, not from the 2005 season finale. Photo: Byron Sullivan / Pexels Rossi’s day was the other story. He fell at high speed in qualifying and started 15th, his lowest grid slot since Qatar 2004. He was up five places at the first corner and eighth by the end of lap one, then moved into third on lap six. He could not close the gap to the two Hondas in the closing laps, but going from 15th on the grid to the podium in 30 laps said plenty about the season he had just had. The finish al

item.title: ‘The Bad Kinda Nepotism,’ ‘This Is So Lame’ – NBA Fans Enraged By Lakers’ Owner Bob Iger’s Son Will’s Latest Move
item.description: ‘The Bad Kinda Nepotism,’ ‘This Is So Lame’ - NBA Fans Enraged By Lakers’ Owner Bob Iger’s Son Will’s Latest Move The Los Angeles Lakers are waiting on new ownership after former Disney CEO Bob Iger and Josh Kushner agreed in August to buy the franchise. Now Iger’s son is set to call games for the team’s G League affiliate, which opens its first season in the Coachella Valley on Friday night. ESPN’s Dave McMenamin relayed the Coachella Valley Lakers’ announcement Thursday that Will Iger will broadcast the team’s games this season. Fans responded by questioning the family connection. Will Iger Joins Coachella Valley Lakers Broadcasts Alongside A.C. Green Will Iger will handle the play-by-play in 2026-27, with A.C. Green beside him as the analyst. Green, who won three championships with the Lakers, did the same job when the team played as the South Bay Lakers. Will Iger’s first broadcast for the club is the season opener against the Salt Lake City Stars. McMenamin led with the family tie when he passed the team’s news along: “Will Iger, the son of incoming Lakers co-owner Bob Iger, will be broadcasting games for LAL’s G League affiliate this season, the Coachella Valley Lakers announced.” The reaction kept returning to the father-son connection, and the word nepotism came up more than once. Less than 20 minutes after McMenamin’s post, one fan wrote, “This the bad kinda nepotism btw.” Another fan saw the hire as a sign of something broader than one G League broadcast booth: “It’s amazing that we’ve gotten to a spot where people don’t even bother to hide the nepotism anymore. It’s become so normalized.” Will Iger does bring play-by-play experience to the role. Before this hire, he called Austin Spurs games, starting in early 2025 for Spurs Sports & Entertainment on FanDuel Sports Network Southwest, and worked some San Antonio FC home matches as well. That job began more than a year before his father agreed to buy into the Lakers. He has called Indoor Football League games since April. His résumé also includes Columbia and Hofstra athletics, high school games in the Austin area and analyst work on The Bounce, the Dallas Mavericks’ weekly show. READ MORE: ‘Feel Bad For Him,’ ‘Gotta Be His Last Year in the NBA’ – Fans React to Lakers Assigning Bronny James to G League Another fan kept the reaction short: “This is so lame lol.” That post drew a reply from another fan, who set the response to Will Iger against the response to Lakers guard Bronny James: “Patiently waiting for the Bronny level outrage (it will never come).” One comparison reached back to the Lakers’ longtime owners, the Buss family. Jerry Buss’s 1979 purchase began more than four decades of family ownership, and after he died in 2013, his six children controlled the team through a trust. “For all of the dysfunction of the Buss family, at least they never selected one of the many siblings with a first name that starts with a J to call games,” another fan wrote. item.title: Lions Trade Idea Could Bring Former Starting Cornerback Back to Detroit
item.description: The Detroit Lions are running out of time to strengthen their secondary before the November 10 NFL trade deadline, but one intriguing possibility could bring a familiar face back to the Motor City. And it’s a player Brad Holmes once traded to acquire. Carlton Davis III , who started 13 games for Detroit during the 2024 season before departing in free agency, has surfaced in NFL trade speculation involving the New England Patriots. According to NFL insider Albert Breer, Davis is among the veterans New England could consider moving before Tuesday’s deadline. That creates an interesting hypothetical reunion for a Lions team still searching for dependable outside cornerback help. But would the Patriots actually trade him, and could Detroit afford to bring him back? Jun 10, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Carlton Davis III (7) speaks to the media after minicamp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) NFL Insider Identifies Carlton Davis as Possible Trade Candidate During a recent appearance on NBC Sports Boston, Breer discussed New England’s potential willingness to move veteran players as the organization considers its long-term roster construction. As Breer explained while discussing the Patriots’ trade possibilities , Davis could become a candidate because of New England’s desire to get younger and accumulate draft capital. The Patriots have several expensive veterans on their roster, and Breer suggested that moving Davis or defensive tackle Christian Barmore wouldn’t necessarily be surprising. However, there’s an important distinction between the two situations. Breer indicated that New England has had trade conversations involving Barmore, while Davis was identified as someone who could potentially become available. There is no confirmed report that the Lions have contacted New England about Davis or that the Patriots have offered him to Detroit. For now, a reunion remains a hypothetical trade idea rather than a developing negotiation. Carlton Davis Already Knows What It Takes to Play in Detroit The biggest argument for bringing Davis back is simple. The Lions already know exactly what they’re getting. Detroit acquired Davis from Tampa Bay in March 2024, surrendering a third-round draft pick while receiving two sixth-round selections as part of the deal. The veteran immediately became an important part of Detroit’s secondary, starting 13 games and recording 56 tackles, two interceptions, and 11 passes defended before a broken jaw ended his season. His physical coverage style fit what the Lions wanted defensively, and his willingness to challenge opposing receivers made him a valuable presence on the outside. Former Lions cornerback Darius Slay even questioned Detroit’s decision to let Davis leave. item.title: Knueppel Injury Deal Another Blow To Hornets’ NBA Cup Hopes
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets are in trouble again. Friday’s NBA Cup game versus the Boston Celtics saw Kon Knueppel ruled out just one day after he finally returned to the court. This news comes straight from the official injury report released Thursday. The second-year sharpshooter played less than six minutes on Wednesday before leaving with a left hamstring strain. Now he sits on the sidelines while the Celtics prepare to visit Spectrum Center. Knueppel’s absence is a disaster for a team already reeling. The 21-year-old missed the first eight games of the season due to the exact same injury. He was supposed to be the spark for an offense that has struggled to find rhythm. Instead, his comeback lasted less than one quarter. Coach Charles Lee offered no timeline for his return after the loss to Brooklyn. “No, I don’t have an update yet,” Lee said afterward, according to Yahoo Sports . A Deep Roster for Boston While Charlotte watches its young star sit, Boston looks ready to roll without its own top guy. Jayson Tatum rested on Wednesday but is expected to play Friday. The Celtics have already proven they can win even when their best player sits out. They beat the Milwaukee Bucks 109-102 on Wednesday night without Tatum. Paul George dropped 25 points and Derrick White added 24 to lead the way. Derrick White stepped up when Payton Pritchard also left the game early with an eye injury. White said his mindset changed when key players went down. “Obviously with JT out and then Payton going out too, I had a little bit more aggressive mind-set,” White said, according to Yahoo Sports . The Celtics believe their depth will carry them through the four-game road trip starting in Charlotte. Hornets Stuck in a Rut Charlotte has lost five games in a row and needs a win badly. They started the season strong with three wins in their first four games but have fallen apart since. The injury to Knueppel makes it nearly impossible to stop Boston’s offense. Brandon Miller struggled mightily on Wednesday, shooting just 2-for-15 from the field. Coach Lee noted that Miller’s defensive effort was still there despite the offensive woes. The Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla praised Paul George’s recent performance. “We need the best version of him for us to be a great team, and I think you were able to see that (Wednesday),” Mazzulla said, according to CBS Sports . Boston enters Friday with a 6-2 record. They are looking to extend their winning streak against a Hornets team that has no answers right now. The loss of Knueppel just confirms what everyone already fears: Charlotte is in deep trouble.

item.title: Elliot Anderson is £116m well spent! Micah Richards explains how England international midfielder has helped to fill Rodri void at Man City
item.description: Elliot Anderson Rodri Manchester City - Getty/GOAL Anderson briefly most expensive British player While nobody was questioning Anderson’s ability after witnessing his meteoric rise from Newcastle’s academy system, through a roller coaster ride at Nottingham Forest and into the heart of the Three Lions’ engine room, eyebrows were raised at his record-setting price tag. The Tyneside native briefly became the most expensive British player of all-time when heading to Manchester, before seeing that entry in the history books erased by the familiar figure of Chelsea-bound Morgan Rogers. Anderson was always going to find himself operating under the brightest of spotlights, with a nine-figure transfer fee bringing with it added expectation. His appearances at the 2026 World Cup promised plenty, but an outing in new colours at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff against Premier League title holders Arsenal delivered some uncomfortable questions. There are not many of those to be found now, with the understated 24-year-old quietly going about his business alongside Erling Haaland and Co. His value to the collective cause is now clear for all to see. Richards' assessment of Anderson at City Richards' assessment of Anderson at City Asked about how impressed he has been with Anderson, former City star Richards - who is putting his contact list to good use again after linking up with Bollington United for a second run through Specsavers’ ‘Best Worst Team’ programme - told GOAL : “If you go back to the Community Shield, I thought he struggled in that game. And I thought, ‘ooh’. “And it's not about the level, obviously he can play at this level, he plays for England, he's a top player. But sometimes it comes down to personality. Can you fit in a team with so many big personalities, full of characters who've already won a lot of things? He's gone there, and after that wobble in the first game, I think he's actually been Man City's best player this season. “Obviously, Haaland scores a lot of the goals, and Haaland does what Haaland does, essentially. I think [Iliman] Ndiaye has done all right coming in. [Jeremy] Doku has played really well in spells. [Rayan] Cherki has been amazing in spells. If you're looking for consistency, whether that be defensive work or going forward, his [Anderson’s] pass the other night for Haaland's goal against Leipzig, it was just unbelievable. I think he's been amazing.” Midfielder can add more goals to his game The good news for City and England is that Anderson can still improve . He only registered six goals through 92 appearances for Forest, and is yet to open his account internationally, with end product being one area to work on. Quizzed on efforts to offer more in the final third, with Rodri chipping in with some vital strikes across his spell at the Etihad, Richards added: “I think he will. I think that comes down to responsibility. “Obviously, when Rodri was in the team, he was a different player. Rodri was more the dictator,

item.title: Alvaro Arbeloa beams as Fulham teenage sensation Josh King earns maiden England call-up from Thomas Tuchel
item.description: Coventry City v Fulham - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has hailed Josh King as the "pride" of the club after the teenage midfielder was handed a shock maiden call-up to the England senior squad. The 19-year-old academy graduate has been selected by Thomas Tuchel for upcoming Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain, marking a historic rise for the Craven Cottage starlet. Arbeloa hails Fulham’s rising star Arbeloa could not hide his delight after watching one of his brightest talents reach the international stage. The former Real Madrid defender turned manager spoke glowingly of the teenager, who has become the first Fulham outfield player to be selected for the Three Lions since Bobby Zamora. The call-up represents a massive milestone for a player who has spent more than a decade developing within the club's youth system. "This is a special moment for him, for us as a club and obviously for our supporters. I think Josh is the pride of our club and our supporters. He came to this club when he was eight years old. And now, when you look at him, how he’s playing, how he’s performing, we are really proud of him. So I think it’s a big step for him. I’m so happy for him because he’s a very humble kid," Arbeloa told Sky Sports . High praise paired with a reality check The Fulham boss believes this is only the beginning for the versatile midfielder, who has already travelled with the senior national team previously without making an appearance. Yet despite beaming with pride over his role in nurturing one of the club's brightest prospects, Arbeloa was quick to sound a vital note of caution, urging the rising star to keep his feet firmly planted on the ground. "You can see every day he wants to improve, he wants to work, he wants to become a better player every day. So I think it’s a special day for him and for all of us. I think he’s on the way to become a star; a very, very important player in this world. I’m so happy that I coached him, helped him to develop and reach his level. But he needs to stay humble like he is," Arbeloa noted. Tuchel explains the shock selection Tuchel has clearly been impressed by more than just the technical ability shown by the 19-year-old during his breakthrough season. The German tactician, who is preparing his side for high-stakes Nations League matches, suggested that King’s character played a pivotal role in his inclusion. While the squad features established stars, Tuchel is keen to reward those showing the right mentality in training and domestic competition. "He is just a fantastic character. He gives us a bit of flexibility. We decided to nominate 22 outfield players for flexibility in training and he is the extra player in training, if you will. He is an exciting player, a versatile player. In pre-season he helped us in training as a full-back, but we will not do that again. It is the attitude and the personality," Tuchel explained. item.title: Sam Mewis makes her picks for 2026 NWSL champion, MVP
item.description: The NWSL playoffs begin this weekend with four quarterfinal matchups: San Diego Wave vs. Utah Royals (Friday, Nov. 6), Kansas City Current vs. Angel City FC (Saturday, Nov. 7), Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign (Sunday, Nov. 8) and Washington Spirit vs. Portland Thorns (Sunday, Nov. 8). Former U.S. women's national team star Sam Mewis, who hosts “The Women’s Game” podcast for the Men In Blazers network, said there’s one particular match she has circled on her calendar. “Kansas City versus Angel City, I had that circled the second that seeding got finalized,” Mewis told USA TODAY Sports in an interview on Nov. 5. “I feel that both teams are actually in really great form coming into playoffs. Among the top teams, I wouldn't want to play against either team. A few of us were saying it's kind of a bummer that this is a first-round game because it feels like a really big one.” Fourth-seeded Kansas City will host the quarterfinal at CPKC Stadium, where the Current have a 32-match regular-season unbeaten streak dating back to July 6, 2024. The magic might not extend to the playoffs, though; the Current lost at home in the 2025 quarterfinals to eventual champion Gotham. Fifth-seeded Angel City , meanwhile, has been on a tear since firing head coach Alexander Straus in June. Days after the coaching change, Angel City also made a mid-season trade with Kansas City to acquire attacker Ally Sentnor, who will face off against her former club in the quarterfinal. Under interim coach Leif Gunnar Smerud, Angel City went undefeated in its final 10 regular-season matches. “There's that expression, the 'new manager bump,’” Mewis said. “Things that were stagnant or not working, players suddenly feel the freedom to do things a little bit differently or respond in a way that they maybe weren't supposed to before. But I think what we're seeing with Angel City is actually really unique, and it feels like everything has come together recently.” Mewis, a three-time NWSL champion with the Western New York Flash and North Carolina Courage, said momentum is an important factor in the postseason. That could be results-based momentum, like San Diego going undefeated in its last seven games and locking up the No. 2 seed. Or it could be emotional momentum, like Seattle playing in honor of captain Jess Fishlock, who plans to retire at the end of the season. As volatile as the playoffs can be, Mewis is predicting that the top two seeded teams will reach the NWSL title game: defending champions and 2026 NWSL Shield winners Gotham FC — whose roster includes Mewis’ sister-in-law Sam Kerr and several USWNT players — and the San Diego Wave. But who will prevail? “It’s hard not to say Gotham,” Mewis said. “I think their roster, their experience, their staff experience at being under pressure — not just this year with a target on their back, but in previous years to have to be an underdog and perform. I think they have a lot of diversity and variety in the way they've been able to find success,

item.title: What channel is UNC-Wofford basketball on Friday night?
item.description: The UNC men's basketball team barely avoided a complete embarrassment during Monday night's season-opener, surviving Western Carolina 80-72. North Carolina (1-0) won Michael Malone's debut behind a balanced scoring attack, strong defense in the closing minutes and second-half free throw shooting. The Catamounts (0-1), facing a huge size disadvantage, out-rebounded the Tar Heels and continued giving themselves several, second-chance opportunities. Next up for UNC: an upset-minded Wofford team that knows how to win in Chapel Hill. The Tar Heels and Terriers will tip off at 7 p.m. on Friday, November 6 inside the Dean Dome. Wofford lost its 2026-27 opener, 90-59, at top-10 Tennessee on Monday. The Terriers (0-1) struggled from the field and free throw line, looking severely out-matched against a team projected to go deep in NCAA Tournament play. North Carolina fans might still have horrors about Wofford, though. The Terriers won in each of their past two trips to Chapel Hill: a 68-64 upset on December 15, 2019, preceded by a 79-75 win on December 20, 2017. UNC needs strong guard play again to win Friday night. Starters Matt Able (18 points), Terrence Brown (14) and Neo Avdalas (13) all scored in double-figures against Western Carolina, while freshman wing Maximo Adams added 10 off the bench. The Tar Heels also need to find solutions down low , with Sayon Keita and Jarin Stevenson expected to carry heavy workloads again. Looking for a fun way to start your weekend? item.title: As LIV Golf burned through cash, a lot of people made a lot of money
item.description: LIV Golf is shutting down after the investment firm that considered giving it $300 million withdrew its offer, forcing the league to begin liquidating its assets. LIV attorney Matthew Williams confirmed Thursday in New Jersey Bankruptcy Court the league will start selling its assets Monday after BC Partners decided it would not invest in LIV 2.0. Why did LIV Golf fail? Inside the nearly $6 billion experiment gone wrong The beginning of the end for the league created by Greg Norman as a competitor to the PGA Tour was when Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund decided in April it could not continue to bankroll a business that offered nothing in return. And it took burning more than $5 billion for the PIF to realize that. Since then, golfers surely tired of CEO Scott O'Neil's outrageous claims and promises, all the while making sure he was taken care of as the ship was sinking. One by one, LIV's biggest assets — its players — bailed. Jumping into a future of uncertainty after being part of the money grab. All the while, O'Neil kept up the charade. After PIF pulled the plug seven months ago, O'Neil said LIV would do "what we do best: putting on the most compelling show in sports." One month ago, he said he believed deeply in the future of LIV and would build something distinctive alongside their players. "We’re delivering on our major milestones," he said. Social media reacts: Here's what people are saying about LIV Golf's demise LIV and BC Partners were seeking 30 to 40 players to compete next season. The Financial Times reported Wednesday about 30 players were currently committed and about 10 were undecided. Marquee names such as Brooks Koepka, Patrick Reed, Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Tyrrell Hatton had departed (Koepka and Reed started the trend early this year). Others such as Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith and Dustin Johnson were among 19 players whose contracts were allowed to be rejected amid bankruptcy and the restructuring process. DeChambeau appeared to be the last holdout, saying on a podcast Oct. 2 he believed LIV 2.0 can make "full financial sense” and hoped it would last forever. LIV indicated it had between $100 million and $500 million in assets and $500 million to $1 billion in liabilities. Lawsuits were piling up from contractors and vendors owed more than $4 million for work this year. That list included Fresh Tape Media, which produced LIV's preseason media days in January held at the Palm Beach County Convention Center. Additionally, 27 players were stiffed out of a combined $64.2 million. O’Neil, though, received more than $13.6 million in payroll, bonuses, benefits, retention payments and expense reimbursements from Sept. 2025 through Aug. 2026. LIV filed for bankruptcy Sept. 8. LIV Golf's business model flawed from start From the start, LIV overshot its mark. The league's objective was to lure deep-pocketed investors for its unconventional team golf format. The plan was for LIV to operate like a professional league with sev

item.title: Ex-Gunner reflects on Arsenal spell ahead of Emirates return with Hull
item.description: Ex-Gunner reflects on Arsenal spell ahead of Emirates return with Hull Hull City’s Brooke Norton-Cuffy has reflected positively on his time with Arsenal, but he’ll be playing to win with his new side on Saturday. Photo by Matt McNulty/Getty Images Former Arsenal academy youngster Brooke Norton-Cuffy returned to England to play in the Premier League this summer, joining Hull City from Genoa . The move was a positive one from an Arsenal perspective, allowing them to cash in on the sell-on clause in Norton-Cuffy’s contract. The Gunners reportedly netted around £2.4m from the deal. But the downside is obviously that Arsenal will now have to play against Norton-Cuffy, with the 22-year-old set to make his first appearance against his old club in their Premier League clash on Saturday. Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images Speaking ahead of the game, Norton-Cuffy insisted he still has many positive memories of his time in north London, although he’ll be returning to the Emirates Stadium looking for three points for Hull. “I look back at my time at Arsenal with fond memor­ies,” Norton-Cuffy said . “I learned a lot. I went from a boy to a man there. “They will have a lot of the ball, but we set up to go into every game to try and win it. I know our team is always going to be on the front foot, aggress­ive, and try­ing to win games.” Photo by George Wood/Getty Images Norton-Cuffy never made a senior competitive debut with Arsenal, despite showing a lot of promise and playing for the academy all the way up to the u21s. Rather than integrating the right-back with the senior side, Arsenal opted to send him out on various loans to Lincoln City , Rotherham United , Coventry City , and Millwall . Those spells went well enough to earn the player that move to Serie A side Genoa, and eventually back to the Premier League. He’s made five appearances for Hull this season, though only one start so far, as he settles in with his new teammates.

item.title: Texas State travels farther and plays later in the Pac-12. Its answer: $1.5M in upgrades
item.description: Texas State head football coach GJ Kinne talks to a reporter during football practice at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, August. 8, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) When Texas State first accepted an invitation to join the Pac-12, excitement blossomed across the program. The future looked bright, but logistically, one particular issue needed to be addressed. Texas State is the only team in the conference located in the Central time zone. How would the Bobcats handle the increased travel costs, especially to the schools in the Pacific Northwest? UP NEXT TEXAS STATE VS. OREGON STATE When/where: 9:30 p.m. Saturday in Corvallis, Ore. TV: CW. Texas State football chief of staff Albert Boone told the American-Statesman earlier this season that he's been pushing for improved travel amenities since his hiring in 2024. His efforts paid off in 2026, as the administration invested nearly $1.5 million in transportation compared to last season. RELATED : Texas State basketball prepares for toughest season in program history "It's about getting the players comfortable. Letting them get their minds right," Boone said. Texas State President Kelly Damphouss said in late June that he, athletic director Don Coryell and their staff spent a lot of time discussing travel. It'll be key again this week as the Bobcats head out for a 1,700-mile trip to Corvallis, Ore. Here's how the athletic department is trying to make those longer journeys more manageable for players: The toll of Texas State's new travel Texas State's 2025 Sun Belt football road trips included Arkansas State, Marshall, Southern Miss and Louisiana-Lafayette. Despite one fewer away game in its Pac-12 debut - San Diego State, Boise State and Oregon State - Texas State is traveling more than an extra 1,000 miles. In addition, the Bobcats have to deal with a time change. Last year, Texas State had no games that started after 7:30 p.m. CT. Their games this season against San Diego State and Boise State started at 9:30 p.m. and 9 p.m. CT, respectively. Saturday's matchup against Oregon State also begins at 9:30 p.m. Texas State flew back the morning after losing to Boise State. Quarterback Brad Jackson said he got back to his apartment Sunday around 7 a.m. following a trip that spanned more than 1,300 miles. "You kind of understand … we're gonna have to sacrifice some of these weeks," Jackson said. Boone said he strongly believes in "you get what you pay for." As the chief of staff, his job is to put the team in the best position to succeed, and subpar travel can impact that. item.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has revived the midnight game launch – but was it worth the wait?
item.description: When our writer found himself among the hundreds on Oxford Street hoping to get their hands on early copies and collectibles, it was a heartwarming reminder of the shared experience of fandom • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come true It is Thursday night and I am sat blurry-eyed and runny nosed outside the Argos on Oxford Street. Incredibly, I am far from alone. This is not some strange protest against the popular retailer. When the clock strikes midnight, the lavish 4K Switch 2 remake of beloved N64 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released, and I have joined a lengthy queue of about 500 fans desperate to snag early copies. There are similar events taking place across the world, from Melbourne to Mexico City; at key locations, Nintendo has senior executives waiting at the tills. These days, of course, most video games are bought as digital copies that download straight to your PC or console on the day of release. You don’t even have to get out of bed to start playing. But in a bygone era, when we used to go to shops to buy games, midnight launches offered a space for likeminded enthusiasts to gather and celebrate their fandom. Every Call of Duty, Halo or Grand Theft Auto release would have fans queueing outside branches of Game or Electronics Boutique, many dressed as favourite characters. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Philly Is The Best Team Right Now’: NBA Legend Makes Bold Sixers Claim On ESPN Tip-Off
item.description: Nov 4, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Philadelphia 76ers center-forward Joel Embiid (21) dribbles defended by Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) in the first half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Benjamin Yu, Editor On Wednesday night’s NBA on ESPN Tip-Off, Shaquille O’Neal made a Sixers claim that would send ripples through NBA social media channels. The Lakers legend claimed, “… Philly is the best team right now” on ESPN Tip-Off. The Sixers went on to prove his point by beating the Detroit Pistons 112-106, behind Jaylen Brown’s 30 points and a clutch block on Pistons star Cade Cunningham late in the fourth quarter. This win improved the Sixers to a league-leading 8-1 record. O’Neal also pointed out how everyone was getting involved, and that could not have been more the case in Wednesday night’s win. Sixers Claim Win Over Pistons After Shaq’s Bold Claim Brown led the team with 30 points, but Joel Embiid was not far behind with 26 of his own, and the seven-foot-two center also grabbed 15 rebounds, which was the 61st occasion of Embiid having a game with at least 25 points and 15 rebounds. Star guard Tyrese Maxey started slow with only two first-half points. However, he turned it on late for 17 in the final two frames, including 11 in the final quarter. That matches his season average in the fourth, which is a testament to Maxey’s sneaky MVP case . LeBron James also had a near triple-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds, and 8 assists, including his 16,000th career field goal , making him the first player in NBA history to reach that mark. Nov 4, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey (0) dribbles defended by Detroit Pistons forward Duncan Robinson (55) in the first half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images The Numbers Behind The 8-1 Start The Sixers’ 8-1 start is their best since the 2023-24 season, when they finished as the Eastern Conference’s seventh seed with a record of 47 wins and 35 losses and were sent home in the first round by the New York Knicks in six games. A more positive stat is that the Sixers have a perfect road record so far with four wins and zero losses. This hasn’t been done in a quarter of a century, when the Sixers were led by MVP Allen Iverson and reached the NBA Finals. In the 26 years since that magical 2000-2001 season, the Sixers have not even reached the conference finals, so hopefully those matching road records are a sign of things to come. Why This Feels Different Than Other Sixers Teams Over the past five to 10 years, the Sixers have usually stalled out early in the playoffs because of a lack of depth. The Sixers were relying on a few players to carry them to victory, which in the playoffs is a recipe for disaster. The Sixers had to rely on Embiid, who was great but often very injured, and they didn’t have the supporting cast around him to get past the second round. This year f

item.title: Packers’ Matt LaFleur reacts to Jordan Love’s Halloween costume
item.description: Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers face a difficult challenge as they try to catch the three teams ahead of them in the NFC North. Despite winning four of their last five games and improving to 5-3, Green Bay remains at the bottom of the division because of the tough competition. The schedule offers little room to relax, with the Packers set to visit the New England Patriots in Week 9 before welcoming the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10. The Packers have been on the receiving end of several controversial penalty calls in recent weeks. Jordan Love and his wife appeared to poke fun at the officiating by dressing as blind NFL referees for Halloween. Although the costumes were likely meant as a joke, the league takes criticism of its officials seriously, particularly when it comes from players or coaches. If the NFL views the outfits as a form of indirect criticism, Love could face a reprimand or a fine. item.title: Right Now Is the Perfect Time to Play the Quietly Best Yakuza Spinoff
item.description: When Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name was released in 2023, the Yakuza series was in a strange position. The team at Sega's Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio was gearing up to give a heroic sendoff to longtime protagonist Kazuma Kiryu. They had big plans for 2024's Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth to pass the torch to a new main character. But Yakuza had unexpectedly become bigger than ever outside Japan, thanks largely to the viral success of Yakuza 0 throughout the late 2010s and early 2020s. The fans demanded more Kiryu, not less. And developer Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio rose to the occasion with The Man Who Erased His Name , an interquel that depicts his lonely years in exile after the events of Yakuza 6.

item.title: Every player from Arkansas to play for the Boston Celtics - Mike Conley
item.description: The Boston Celtics have traded for, signed, and drafted players from nearly every U.S. state and countries across the globe. From Alabama to Yugoslavia, the Celtics have a history of thoroughly seeking talent to succeed in the NBA. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor league of the NBA) in the earliest years of the Association, the organization has tirelessly searched for talent since its inception. In this installment of our series documenting the origins of every player who has represented the Celtics, we will focus on players from Arkansas who have played for Boston. Our focus in this article is Mike Conley. An alum of Ohio State, he was picked up with the fourth overall selection of the 2007 NBA Draft by the Memphis Grizzlies . The Fayetteville, Arkansas native played the first 12 seasons of his pro career with Memphis. He also played for the Utah Jazz and Minnesota Timberwolves before he signed with the Boston Celtics in 2026. He remains with the team at the time of writing. During his time suiting up for the Celtics, Conley put up 6.0 points and 2.0 steals per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Which Stars Will Be Dealt Before the NFL Trade Deadline? Analysts Predict the Biggest Names to Get Moved
item.description: Which Stars Will Be Dealt Before the NFL Trade Deadline? Analysts Predict the Biggest Names to Get Moved The 2026 NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching. Teams have until Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET to make moves, and NFL insiders are predicting that there could be quite a few deals prior to the deadline. There have already been plenty of fireworks in recent weeks, with notable players like Jeffery Simmons (Chicago Bears), Quenton Nelson (Seattle Seahawks), DeForest Buckner (San Francisco 49ers), Joey Porter Jr. (Dallas Cowboys), Marvin Harrison Jr. (Houston Texans), Cam Jurgens (Baltimore Ravens), Jacoby Brissett (Ravens), and J.J. McCarthy (New York Giants) already traded. Who will be the biggest stars traded in the next few days? Pro Football Network asked our NFL analysts to share their predictions for the 2026 trade deadline. NFL Analysts Predict the Biggest Stars Who Will Be Traded Prior to Nov. 10 Deadline Jacob Infante : “I expect Jonathan Taylor to be traded before the NFL trade deadline. The Colts are clearly in rebuilding mode after trading both DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson, and Taylor is arguably their most valuable asset to trade. Contenders like the Vikings, Seahawks, and Patriots would make perfect sense as potential landing spots for Taylor.” Ben Rolfe : “Khalil Mack deserves a chance to go and play for a contender. Exactly where he goes is fairly wide open. Most contending teams could take on a rotational EDGE rusher, especially one that comes with a $4.0 million cap hit after Week 9. There is no real reason to think Mack could not contribute in a number of spots and be an impact player in a playoff run.” Kyle Soppe : “Jonathan Taylor is the biggest name, but the biggest impact might well be Josh Sweat. There’s no real bad fit for a star player like this who comes preloaded with postseason experience and has the versatility to impact any system. We know that the QB position is the most important in the sport, and making them comfortable/uncomfortable is a top priority. That means skill guys and pass rushers will always be valuable. “The only issue here is predicting the Cardinals to be forward-thinking, and that feels like a long shot. But if they are willing to admit where they are, they can gain future win equity by way of a player whose timeline isn’t the same as theirs.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Jason Katz : “Despite the Colts looking like the worst team in football, I still think Jonathan Taylor ends up staying. I just don’t think the Colts end up getting the exorbitant price they are asking for. The biggest name may end up being a defensive player, but I’m going to focus on the offensive side of the ball and say Brian Thomas Jr. “I am still more of a believer in him than not. item.title: 2026 Week 10 Preview: Rice Owls @ North Texas Mean Green
item.description: DENTON, TX - OCTOBER 29: North Texas Mean Green quarterback Tayven Jackson (2) scrambles for a first down during the game between the North Texas Mean Green and the Florida Atlantic Owls on October 29, 2026 at DATCU Stadium in Denton, TX. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Game notes Time and date: Saturday, November 7 at 4:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPNU Location: DATCU Stadium — Denton, TX Spread: North Texas (-17.5) Over/under: 64.5 All-time series: North Texas leads, 9-5 Last meeting: North Texas 56, Rice 24 — November 22, 2025 Current streak: North Texas, 4 (2020-25) Setting the scene As of Friday, Nov. 6, only one team is perfect in the American Conference standings. North Texas carries a five-game win streak and a 4-0 conference record into a home matchup against Rice. While the Owls have yet to defeat an FBS opponent and ride a seven-game losing streak, they have competed against the American’s best throughout the season — falling 16-14 to UTSA and 51-49 at Florida Atlantic. North Texas hopes to avoid a scare and continue its trek toward a second-straight American Championship Game appearance under two different coaching staffs. The Mean Green have dominated the series this decade, winning all four matchups since 2020. Rice Owls outlook Rice (1-7, 0-4 American) is the only team in the American awaiting its first conference victory. The Owls have come excruciatingly close several times, including last outing at Florida Atlantic, where its game-winning field goal attempt fell inches short of the uprights. The Owls unlocked something special in that loss in Boca Raton. Backup quarterback Gael Ochoa, making his first collegiate start, put up historic numbers. He rushed for 259 yards on 12 attempts, setting the American Conference single-game record for rushing average at 21.6 yards per carry. Ochoa produced four touchdowns — all spanning at least 50 yards — and recorded the most rushing yards by a quarterback since Bert Emanuel Jr. of Central Michigan in 2022. However, the bye week allowed time for starter Jacurri Brown to recover. Now Rice has two effective mobile quarterbacks and must figure out how to manage them. Brown has eclipsed 120 yards rushing in three games this season, including 155 in his last start against Tulsa on Oct. 17. Head coach Scott Abell did not reveal his gameplan, but both quarterbacks could see substantial action against North Texas. The quarterbacks have benefited from quality run blocking, led by guard Patrick Valent. The Owls’ option attack ranks fourth in the country in rushing yards per game, ninth in rushing average, and first in 40-yard pickups. One reason Rice’s offense had more success against Florida Atlantic than other opponents was the contribution from other sources. Running back Tyvonn Byars produced 93 yards that day, and he is heating up with 257 yards across his last three games. Slot receiver Max Mosey added a season-high 84 rushing yards, allowin

item.title: Beau Ankeney mashed his way onto the prospect radar in 2026
item.description: PHOENIX, AZ - MARCH 29: Beau Ankeney (35) Grand Canyon Infielder takes a big swing during a baseball game between the Arizona Wildcats and the Grand Canyon Lopes on March 29, 2022, at GCU Ballpark in Phoenix, AZ. (Photo by Zac BonDurant/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There are two particular categories of player that go under the radar in the major league amateur draft each year. The first are college seniors. If you didn’t get drafted by your junior year or earlier, as a JUCO or prep player, there’s a natural stigma attached. The second are first basemen. Because the position is usually filled by less athletic players whose value is heavily tied up in their bat, only the top ranked college first baseman really get much notice, and they tend to go in the early rounds as some of the better hitters each year. Leaving aside the player and just considering the profile, Spencer Torkelson was a hard player to philosophically wrap one’s head around as the first overall pick in the draft back in 2020. Living up to that would’ve required him to develop quickly into one of the better hitters in baseball. There’s a reason you very rarely see a 1-1 first baseman. Detroit Tigers prospect Beau Ankeney checks both boxes, and he definitely didn’t get much attention on draft day 2025 when they picked him in the 14th round out of Loyola Marymount and paid him just the minimum signing bonus. He played three years at Grand Canyon University before breaking out and transferring to Loyola for his senior season in 2025. That was notable, as he was clearly a bit of a late bloomer. Also notable was his muscular six-foot-three, 235 pound frame. He only played in four games after the draft, so there wasn’t anything to get excited about yet. That changed in 2026. Ankeney mashed 24 home runs total, including 9 in just 27 games at the High-A level after he was promoted in late July. He took his walks. He showed pretty good athleticism for a first baseman, with enough speed to handle a corner outfield spot here and there. His raw power really stood out, as he averaged 92 mph off the bat, which is great even at the MLB level, and maxed out at 114.4 mph off the bat, giving him a 65 FV grade on his raw power potential. And most importantly, he took his walks and didn’t strike out that much for a power hitter. In Lakeland at Single-A, Ankeney chased about 30 percent of the time, and his whiff rate was similarly on the higher end of the scale. Considering that he was 23 years old already and competing with 19-22 year old players quite a bit, it was impressive, but didn’t really knock anyone’s socks off. What really got prospect hounds talking was the fact that he went straight into High-A and did even more damage, without much of an increase in his strikeout rate. From August 4 through the 16th, Ankeney hit seven homers in nine games while walking and racking up one multi-hit game after another. He was the hottest hitter in the league for that

item.title: Morning Report: Henry Cejudo suggests UFC release Conor McGregor instead of paying for final fight
item.description: ﻿Conor McGregor | Ian Maule, Getty Images Conor McGregor plans to fight out his UFC contract soon, but could the promotion have other plans for him? That’s what former two-division champion Henry Cejudo suggests is a possibility, given McGregor’s notoriously high salary and his guarantee that he will move on to bare-knuckle boxing for BKFC once his UFC run is over. Cejudo wonders why the UFC doesn’t just cut ties with him now and be done with it. “At this point, he’s just f*cking trolling,” Cejudo said on his Pound 4 Pound podcast. “I don’t believe anything that he’s saying. But he’s a draw, you know? Now it’s up to the UFC to say, ‘Hey, we’re going to pay you this much because you’re worth this much.’ I guarantee, I’m going to tell you right now, I can even see the UFC just letting him go based on what he got paid. They could be like, ‘Hey, you know what? You’ve got one fight left. We don’t think you’re worth that. You’re a free agent.’ “If I’m a businessman and I want to keep a lot of my money, and I like Conor—f*ck Conor. I would cut him. I swear to you I would, because if they’re going to give him 30 million and not have to give him 30 million particularly with that big-ass Paramount deal that they have and Paramount has to make their money, hey, just cut him. Let him be a free agent. Let him make more money elsewhere, but let him not make money or take money from us.” McGregor is the biggest box office draw in the history of the UFC, and also took part in a crossover boxing match with Floyd Mayweather Jr. in 2017 that generated over four million pay-per-view buys. However, his reputation has plummeted in recent years due to a lack of success in the cage—McGregor is just 1-4 in the UFC since the Mayweather fight—and his deplorable behavior outside of it, including being found liable for sexual assault in 2024. This past July at UFC 329, McGregor returned from a five-year hiatus to face rival Max Holloway, but the bout ended in just 69 seconds due to McGregor suffering a leg injury—the same injury that initially put him on the shelf for an extended period of time. Cejudo isn’t sure if the McGregor experience is worth it anymore. “There’s no more pay-per-view model, and this dude hasn’t won a fight,” Cejudo said. “Just the business aspect of it, just hear me out. Pretend I’m Dana White, you know what I’m doing? I’m saying he’s got one fight left, his last fight wasn’t even a fight. He lost again. Just let him leave with the loss in the UFC. Let him start his own career. Let us not pay him what he’s worth, which is $30 million—I believe he got paid $30 million in this fight against Holloway. That’s what he used to generate. There’s no more pay-per-views. … These contracts are already done. “It’s not because, ‘Oh, Conor McGregor’s going to do this, give us more money.’ These contracts are already said and done.” Cejudo added that there’s a risk in McGregor facing one of the UFC’s stars, picking up a win to boost his value once more, and then head

item.title: 6 cooked NBA teams already serving up a lost season
item.description: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NBA’s 82-game regular season leaves plenty of margin for error for a bad stretch of play. This is a league where 53% of teams make the playoffs, not counting the four other teams who have the opportunity to earn their way into the postseason with one or two wins in the play-in tournament. There are still five months left on the schedule, with back-to-backs and spells of three-games-in-four-nights filling in the calendar. Most teams can get off to a bad start and still be just fine. Some teams already know their season is over before it ever really starts. Check out our NBA power rankings this week for full coverage of the league . Just over two weeks into the season, it already feels like there are six teams who are already toast. Some of these teams knew they would be bad coming into the year, while others dreamed of breaking into the playoffs. The unfortunate reality for these teams is they can’t even count on a high draft pick next year anymore after the league’s anti-tanking lottery reform was put in place this season ahead of the 2027 draft. Of course, there’s plenty of time for things to change with only about 10% of the schedule complete, but these six teams already look cooked. Sacramento Kings The Kings appeared to have no hope coming into the season, and at this point the only intrigue left is to see if they avoid being the worst team of the 2020s, a stake currently held by the 14-win Detroit Pistons in 2023-24. Rookie guard Darius Acuff is the best thing this franchise has going for them, and he’s getting thrown into the deep end from the very start of his career. Acuff leads the NBA in minutes per game and he’s one field goal attempt behind 2-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for the league-lead in that category. The Kings could probably stand to give some of Acuff’s usage (32.5%) to Domantas Sabonis (16.1% usage rate), but they would still be a bad team, and at least now the rookie guard has the ability to learn from his mistakes. Keegan Murray being out again with an ankle injury after only playing 23 games last year is the real bummer for the start of this season. The Kings felt like the worst team in the league entering the season, and they still feel like the worst team in the league. Try to enjoy the Acuff roller coaster, Kings fans, because there’s nothing else to latch onto. Chicago Bulls The good news is that rookie forward Caleb Wilson looks like he can be the franchise player the Bulls have been missing since their horrible Jimmy Butler trade 10 years ago. The bad news is they might need four new starters around him long-term. It’s been a truly disappointing start for Matas Buzelis, who looked like a keeper in his first two seasons under Billy Donovan, but is regressing and seemingly falling out of favor under new head coach Tiago Splitter. Buzelis’ inability to beat mismatches when teams put their tiny guards on him is the single most alarming trend of this sea

item.title: Staff Predictions: Michigan Football vs MSU
item.description: Oct 25, 2025; East Lansing, Michigan, USA; Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood (19) reacts after scoring a touchdown against the Michigan State Spartans during the first half at Spartan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brendan Mullin-Imagn Images | Brendan Mullin-Imagn Images The Michigan Wolverines return to The Big House this weekend to take on their in-state rivals, the Michigan State Spartans. In this week’s Roundtable, Maize n Brew staff members give some takeaways from last week’s game, some bold predictions for tomorrow’s game and more! As always, let’s reflect on last week’s game. Provide any takeaways you had from the Rutgers game. Von : That was WAY too close for comfort. The offense actually put together a solid game from start to finish, but it was the defense and special teams that made the game at Rutgers be much closer than it should have been. Giving up an 80-yard touchdown pass to Rutgers is embarrassing enough, but to let that happen against its backup quarterback? Come on, man. As far as special teams go, Trey Butkowski is broken after missing four of his last six field goals. These types of things should not be happening on a Kyle Whittingham-led team, but it’s not surprising at this point, as stuff like this has been happening all year long. Kellen : My biggest takeaway is that we learned that Tommy Carr is a good enough quarterback to make up for mediocre play calling. Grace : Tommy Carr made some great plays and I think Michigan decided to establish some sort of passing identity. The receivers and tight ends made some plays, and it’s a good sign Michigan was able to score a few touchdowns. I’m still nervous about the inability to run the ball, especially given the teams remaining on Michigan’s schedule. Matt : We didn’t learn much, but the offense’s inability to run the ball against arguably the worst rushing defense in the country is concerning. Don’t let the 161 rushing yards fool you — a large portion of those were Tommy Carr scrambles on broken plays. Michigan’s offense still has severe flaws and the Rutgers game didn’t do anything to assuage those fears. Scotty : Tommy Carr looked great. Yes, it was Rutgers, but that was his second start. Great to see. On the flip side, I have no idea how this team manages to keep games like that close. Very concerning. Charles : The offense still has a very, very long way to go to be competent, but it did show progress and seems to be operating at a higher level with Tommy Carr. The freshman quarterback was a real bright spot in his second career start and should continue to get better. Unfortunately, the defense uncharacteristically gave up a few big plays, and Trey Butkowski missed two field goals for a second straight week, so Rutgers was able to keep it close. In order to finish the season on a positive note, Michigan has to find a way to play well in all three phases, which hasn’t happened all season. item.title: Houston Texans return to Pee Wee Ball drills to fix defense before Chargers game
item.description: Houston Texans linemen watch Houston Texans place kicker Ka'imi Fairbairn (15) 58-yard field goal against the New York Giants in the first half of game action at Reliant Stadium in Houston on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) The first set of drills at the Houston Texans ' first practice after a week off focused on the basics. Coach DeMeco Ryans led the instruction. One group of defensive players knelt in a row on the 35-yard line while another group stood in front of them. When Ryans yelled, "Drive," the players on their knees wrapped up the ones standing and squeezed. "He took us back to Pee Wee Ball today," star edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. said with a laugh. The drill was aimed at improving one of the things that has plagued the Texans' defense this season and contributed to their loss to the Giants two weeks ago: missed tackles. Ryans hopes the emphasis will lead to better play from a defensive unit that has largely underperformed this season . The Texans have given up extra yards and explosive plays because they haven't tackled well. The drill was one way to address the problem. "It's just a matter of emphasizing things, areas where we need to improve as coaches, as players," Ryans said after practice. "We just emphasize it, put our focus there. We want to see it get better on Sunday." It'll be one of the keys in Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Texans have an opportunity to right the ship Sunday . A win could help spark a run. A loss could have devastating consequences, potentially ending their pursuit of the playoffs and causing general manager Nick Caserio and Ryans to rethink their approach to the Nov. 10 trade deadline . The Texans have no room for error. The Chargers are the only team in the NFL without a win. If there's one game that could help get the Texans' defense back on track, it should be this one. The Chargers' offense ranks last in the league in points per game (14.1). It leads the league with 17 giveaways - 10 interceptions and seven fumbles. And quarterback Justin Herbert is having the worst statistical season of his career. It's the perfect game for a defense that has struggled to generate turnovers and ranks tied for 29th in the league. Ryans had a completely different perspective on the Chargers, though. He called them "a really good football team," even if their record doesn't suggest it. "Their quarterback is a really great player, their defense has been really good," Ryans said. "They eliminate explosives. This is a really good team. We don't come in looking at the record and making any predetermined notions of who this team is. "We go out, we watch the film, we prepare for a really good team." But this week's game, players say, is less about the opponent and more about fixing the things they've struggled with this year. item.title: Inter List Liverpool Misfit and Several Young Attackers
item.description: Inter List Liverpool Misfit and Several Young Attackers Inter are contemplating fortifying their attack, but it won’t necessarily happen in January, unless a tasty opportunity falls into their lap. The Nerazzurri are more focused on the long term, Tuttomercatoweb reports. They and Juventus are very keen on Samuele Inacio, but he’s unlikely to leave Borussia Dortmund before he fully blooms and his price tag balloons. He has made just four senior-team appearances this season. Inter are also tracking Paul Mendy, who recently renewed his Cagliari contract, and Jay Robinson , who’s on loan from Southampton to Monza. As for January, Federico Chiesa could be an option if he ever decides the time has come for him to leave Liverpool. He has featured just once this campaign due to recurring physical problems. He’s been available for only three contests. Despite the constant chatter linking him to a Serie A return, he’s been reluctant to flee Anfield. Instead, Giacomo Raspadori could be easier to sign, as he’s not a fixture under Maurizio Sarri. He’s duplicative with Charles De Ketelaere and didn’t pan out on the wings, where he’s been lapped by Jonathan Rowe, Elijf Elmas, and Nicola Zalewski. He too has missed time due to injury, notching two goals and one assist in seven outings. Atalanta paid €22M to acquire him from Atletico Madrid last January. Our Take on the Inter Front-Line Chances are they’ll do something only if one of their four options gets hurt. They should go young eventually. Luring Chiesa would be interesting because of his versatility, but he has a very high salary. It’s been a minute since he’s been an impact player. Raspadori has had success as a super sub, but there’s a reason teams keep passing him around.

item.title: Rutgers Football History vs. Wisconsin Shows Another Lopsided Matchup
item.description: CHESTNUT HILL, MA - SEPTEMBER 11: Greg Schiano of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights encourages his team during a game between the Rutgers Scarlet Knights and the Boston College Eagles at Alumni Stadium on September 11, 2026 in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts. (Photo by Burt Granofsky/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Another week, another lopsided matchup for Greg Schiano and the Scarlet Knights. Rutgers will travel to Madison to take on Wisconsin on Saturday. The Badgers are coming off a 30-0 loss suffered against Iowa after finally cracking in the Top 25 poll. The last thing Wisconsin needs is a home loss to an injured Rutgers team. The trend has favored Wisconsin as the team has always had a size and physicality edge against Rutgers — and the results show it. The Scarlet Knights will be without starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan once again. KJ Duff was listed as doubtful on Wednesday’s injury report, meaning the offense will be without one of the best receivers in the nation. This does not bode well for a team that would already enter at a disadvantage at full strength. Rutgers Football History vs. Wisconsin Rutgers and Wisconsin first played in 2014 when the Scarlet Knights made the move to the Big Ten. These two teams have played six games over the years with all meetings going the way of the Badgers. All have been decided by double digits with just two games being decided by less than 20 points. Wisconsin has outscored Rutgers, 234-50. The closest game Rutgers played came in 2023 when it traveled to Madison against a flawed Wisconsin team. The Badgers were still able come away with a 24-13 win. Here is how each game has played out: Nov. 1, 2014: Wisconsin 37, Rutgers 0 Oct. 31, 2015: Wisconsin 48, Rutgers 10 Nov. 3, 2018: Wisconsin 31, Rutgers 17 Nov. 6, 2021: Wisconsin 52, Rutgers 3 Oct. 7, 2023: Wisconsin 24, Rutgers 13 Oct. 12, 2024: Wisconsin 42, Rutgers 7 Rutgers and Wisconsin will kick off at 4:14pm on Saturday.

item.title: The Denver Broncos Coaches Who Built the Standard a Mile High
item.description: “Thanks, Dan, for giving me an opportunity in the NFL.” – A (hopefully) future Hall of Fame coach On Thursday, the Pro Football Hall of Fame announced five coaching candidates still in contention for its Class of 2027. Bill Belichick, Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves, and Mike Shanahan. Five men who have collectively made an awful lot of football fans very happy or wholly infuriated. For Broncos fans, two of those names brought a lot of joy and carry a particular bit of weight. And while only one of the five will advance to the final round of consideration later this month, it’s worth spending a little time appreciating just how much those two men gave to a franchise that has spent much of the last half-century expecting to be amongst the best in football. Because those expectations didn’t come from nowhere. I was a young kid when the Broncos made their first Super Bowl appearance in January 1978. My family had moved to California a few years earlier, and I remember feeling very far away from Colorado, perhaps for the first time. I’d gotten Lyle Alzado’s signature while I was home visiting my dad at Summer Camp in 1977, at the beginning of that huge year, and there was something about watching Red Miller, Craig Morton, and that remarkable Orange Crush defense representing the place I still thought of as home that made those miles feel a little longer. Maybe a lot longer. The Broncos lost to Dallas that day, 27-10. It was a tough introduction to the particular heartbreak of being a Denver football fan, though we’d eventually become pretty damned proficient at that particular exercise. But Red Miller had done something extraordinary. He’d taken a franchise that had never even reached the playoffs to 12-2, and brought it all the way to the Super Bowl. He’d shown us what was possible. Dan Reeves was the man who made us believe that possibility could happen again. And again. And again. I’d just moved home to Colorado when Reeves arrived in Denver in 1981, a 37-year-old former Dallas Cowboys player and assistant who had already experienced championship football from both sides of the sideline. Within a few years, he’d helped bring John Elway to Denver, and the two began one of the most successful, occasionally contentious partnerships in Broncos history. Over 12 seasons, Reeves won 110 regular-season games, five division titles, and three AFC championships. His teams reached the playoffs six times and suffered only two losing seasons. Most remarkably, those three Super Bowl appearances came in a four-year stretch, against the Giants, Washington, and San Francisco. They lost all three. Sometimes spectacularly. I remember watching just how damned spectacularly. And yet, think about what that represented. Before Reeves, the Broncos had reached one Super Bowl in their entire existence. They couldn’t keep that momentum, a big part of what brought Reeves there. By the end of the 1980s under Reeves, getting there had become something approaching an exp

item.title: ‘They killed James Harden for it’: Doc Rivers says nobody talked about what Luka Doncic kept on doing
item.description: Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images Luka Doncic and James Harden share a similar playing style. The Los Angeles Lakers and Cleveland Cavaliers stars share a heliocentric, high-usage and step-back-heavy style, and that makes them both brilliant. However, Doc Rivers, who coached Harden and watched his team play against Doncic, has claimed that the two players are actually very different. But they did share one similarity for which only Harden was criticised, says Rivers. Doc Rivers says Luka Doncic got away with holding the ball but James Harden didn’t Rivers coached Harden with the Philadelphia 76ers between 2022 and 2023. Despite the obvious similarities everyone talks about, the 65-year-old claimed that they are not alike at all – except for the fact that they both hold onto the ball ‘forever’. Rivers claimed that Harden was blasted for doing it, but Doncic constantly got away with it, even though he did it a lot more. On his podcast , when Ben Simmons spoke about Harden and Doncic’s similar heliocentric style of play, Rivers replied: “He’s different. They are different. Even though they both hold the ball forever. “Even in Luka’s heyday in Dallas, people never talked about it, but they killed James Harden for having the ball, but Luka actually had the ball more in his hands, and no one ever said that, which is really interesting. “It is different. They are similar in the way they hold the ball. It feels like Luka does the action quicker than James. They both are extraordinary passers.” Harden was definitely criticised, but Doncic didn’t completely get away with it. Both players got their share of stick from fans, pundits and the media for holding on to the ball. Now, Doncic plays for the Lakers and Harden for the Cavaliers, and both players have evolved their games compared to a few years ago. Neither is as heliocentric as they were in the past. item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - MAY 04: Jac Caglianone #14 of the Kansas City Royals is doused with water by Bobby Witt Jr. #7 and Carter Jensen #22 of the Kansas City Royals after a 6-2 win over the Cleveland Guardians at Kauffman Stadium on May 04, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Ed Zurga/Getty Images) | Getty Images Max wrote about yesterday’s biggest stories already: Royals add Hunter Mense as assistant hitting coach ( MLB.com story ) Three Royals named Silver Slugger finalists ( MLB.com story ) Jaylon Thompson writes about both for The Star. About Mense : Mense was a minor-league hitting coordinator in the Blue Jays organization. He became an assistant hitting coach at the big-league level in 2022. He has worked alongside such All-Stars as Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and George Springer. The Royals have been looking to backfill their lineup of hitting coaches. Last month they reassigned Alec Zumwalt to the minor leagues. His departure left the open spot on Matt Quatraro’s coaching staff that Mense is set to fill. About Silver Slugger : The Kansas City Royals had three of the top hitters in the American League this season. And on Thursday, that trio was recognized as Louisville Slugger Silver Slugger Award finalists at each player’s respective position. Royals star Bobby Witt Jr. headlined the club’s finalists. He joins Jac Caglianone and Carter Jensen as award nominees. Caglianone is an outfield finalist and Jensen — who is coming off his rookie season — is a finalist behind the plate. Also at The Star, Pete Grathoff points to a writer who thinks Jac has a lot to lose from the lockout: The New York Times reported that teams have been instructed to “document interactions between players and medical/training staff during the latter part of the season to confirm that there have not been any disabling injuries prior to the end of the season.” That lack of medical care is one reason why RotoWire’s Thomas Leary believes a lockout could affect Royals outfielder Jac Caglianone more than other players. Darragh McDonald at MLBTR also writes about Mense : [Mark] Feinsand [of MLB.com] further clarifies that Mense and Marcus Thames will be the hitting coaches in Kansas City while Connor Dawson will be offensive coordinator. In 2026, Thames and Dawson worked as hitting coaches alongside Alec Zumwalt. It was reported in September that Zumwalt would be reassigned to a position as senior director of hitting performance. McDonald also had an old friend alert : The White Sox have signed right-hander Alec Marsh to a minor league contract with an invite to major league camp in spring training. Scott Merkin of MLB.com was among those to report the deal. item.title: Arsenal could make January move for Juventus star
item.description: Arsenal could make January move for Juventus star Kenan Yildiz has emerged as one of the most exciting attacking talents in European football, with the Turkish youngster becoming a central figure at Juventus. However, his impressive development has also attracted interest from Arsenal , who would love to bring him to the Emirates Stadium. Yildiz came through the youth ranks at Bayern Munich before Juventus secured his services and offered him a pathway into their first team. That decision has proved successful, with the attacker developing into one of the most influential players in the Italian side’s squad. His performances have caught Arsenal’s attention, and the Gunners have reportedly monitored him for some time. His ability to operate on the left wing and make an impact in attack makes him an appealing option as they consider ways to strengthen their forward line. Arsenal continue to monitor Juventus star Yildiz has been on Arsenal’s transfer list over the last two seasons, but Juventus have shown little willingness to let him leave . The Italian club consider him one of their most important players and are determined to keep him in Turin. Nevertheless, Arsenal will know that even highly valued players can become available if the right offer arrives. Juventus may be reluctant to sell, but a sufficiently attractive proposal could test their resolve. The bigger question is whether the Italian side would even consider losing such an important player halfway through the season. Arsenal are currently looking at attacking reinforcements ahead of the January transfer window, making the timing of any potential approach particularly significant. Kenan Yildiz (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Yildiz among Arsenal’s January targets According to Mirror Football , Yildiz is one of the players Arsenal would like to add to their squad when the transfer window reopens in the new year. The report underlines the Gunners’ interest in strengthening their attacking options, although convincing Juventus to negotiate could prove difficult. The Turkish international is an important part of their plans, and they would have little reason to weaken their squad during the campaign. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Max Power: NASA hosting its 1st air show this weekend on Florida's Space Coast
item.description: null NASA will host a first-of-its-kind air show and aerospace expo on Florida's Space Coast this weekend. The show, called Max Power, will take place Saturday and Sunday (Nov. 7 and Nov. 8) at and around NASA's Kennedy Space Center (KSC). That name should be familiar to "Simpsons" fans, by the way: Max Power is an alias that Homer uses in the 13th episode of the show's 10th season. (He got it off a hair dryer.) There will be a lot to see at NASA's event, so you should consider dropping by if you're on the Space Coast this weekend. (Tickets are required; you can buy them here .) Here are a few of the highlights. Saturday, Nov. 7 (all times local, EST): 11:15-11:30 a.m.: Overview of NASA's "quiet" supersonic jet, the X-59 12:30-1:00 p.m.: Discussion of NASA's science and exploration goals by Nicky Fox and Lori Glaze (the heads of NASA's Science Mission Directorate and Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate, respectively) 12:45-1:00 p.m.: Q&A with the four astronauts of NASA's Artemis III mission 1:00-1:30 p.m.: "How Is NASA Preparing Astronauts to Live and Work on the Moon?" with Suzanne Bell, who leads NASA’s Behavioral Health and Performance Laboratory at Johnson Space Center 1:30-2:00 p.m.: Discussion of NASA's planned lunar outpost , with Moon Base program head Carlos García-Galán 2:00-2:30 p.m.: Summary of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope mission, by senior project scientist Julie McEnery Sunday, Nov. 8 11:15-11:30 a.m.: "How NASA uses aircraft for research! Topic: Connecting flight to research" 12:45-1:15 p.m.: Update on the U.S. Space Academy with NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson 12:45-1:00 p.m. (different stage): Q&A with NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station 1:00-1:30 p.m.: Discussion of SR-1 Freedom, NASA's planned nuclear-powered spacecraft that will launch mini-helicopters to Mars in 2028 1:30-2:00 p.m.: "The X-Factor: NASA's Flight Revolution Topic: X-Planes" 2:00-2:30 p.m.: Conversation with an (as yet unnamed) NASA astronaut 3:00-3:15: "In the Cockpit: Meet the NASA Pilots!" NASA's Freedom 250 F-5 team, including NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, performs a flyover during the national anthem at an NFL game between the Cleveland Browns and the Carolina Panthers in Cleveland on Sept. 27, 2026. (Image credit: NASA/Jordan Cochran) NASA will also hold a livestreamed press conference on Saturday at 5 p.m. EST (2200 GMT) about its moon base plans. It will feature Fox, García-Galán, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and Dayna Ise, the acting director of the Utility and Infrastructure Office for the Moon Base Program. There will also be dramatic flyovers on both days of Max Power, some of them by Isaacman, who's an accomplished pilot as well as a private astronaut.
